sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Django is in more Python backend job descriptions than any other framework. Freshers are expected to know the MTV pattern, migrations, and the ORM basics — even if they've only used it in a college project.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Django's MTV vs MVC mapping:**

| MVC | Django MTV | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Model | Model | Data layer, database schema |
| View | Template | Presentation/HTML |
| Controller | View | Request handling, business logic |

Django calls the controller a 'View'. Confusing at first, critical to get right in interviews.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Project vs App** — project is the entire site configuration (`settings.py`, root `urls.py`). App is a reusable component (`models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`).
- **Migrations** — `makemigrations` creates migration files from model changes; `migrate` applies them to the database. Both are needed.
- **ORM basics** — `Model.objects.all()`, `.filter(field=value)`, `.get(pk=1)`, `.create(...)`, `.save()`, `.delete()`.
- **`urls.py`** — URL routing. `path('users/', views.user_list)` maps URL to view function.
- **`settings.py`** — `DEBUG`, `DATABASES`, `INSTALLED_APPS`, `SECRET_KEY`. Never commit SECRET_KEY.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the difference between makemigrations and migrate?'** — makemigrations generates files from model changes; migrate runs them against the database.
- **'What is MTV?'** — Model (data), Template (presentation), View (logic). The controller is the View in Django.
- **'What is the difference between a project and an app in Django?'** — project is the deployment unit; app is a reusable feature module.
- **'How do you query all records from a model?'** — `MyModel.objects.all()`.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"Django follows the MTV pattern where the View is what MVC calls a controller. I define models as Python classes, run makemigrations to generate the migration files, then migrate to apply them. The ORM lets me write MyModel.objects.filter(status='active') instead of raw SQL — Django generates the query safely with parameterised placeholders."*
